decisions.reason: The rejection treats R as the object braiding, but def-qc-tqc-r-symbol Definition explicitly defines R as the matrix of f ↦ f ∘ c_{x,x}^{-1}. Thus inverse precomposition is already included in R_i; replacing it by R_i^{-1} would reverse the stated convention. F recoupling gives T_i^{-1} R_i T_i, with the specified column-vector product order. The nonzero simple-charge domain and owning contract/page agree. No source edit is warranted.

F2 omitted the published operator-norm definition’s zero-domain branch, and the original maximum-over-unit-vectors proof did not cover the stated V=0 case. Both error maps are then zero; the repair handles this case explicitly, retains the full theorem, and proves the remaining contraction bounds using ||Ay||≤||A|| ||y|| including y=0. This is a nonfatal boundary omission, not a false theorem.

The PU(V) equivalence relation, attained minimum, representative independence, symmetry, triangle inequality and separation are sound for V≠0, including dim V=1. The braid-gate title/interface lacked its explicit specialization to the declared braid-action supplier. Added only the projective braid gate [rho_c(b)] in the same quotient; no metric, common-phase convention or hypothesis changed.

The actual Statement and word-by-word proof correctly give the common scalar character chi(b)=R_1^{e(b)}, including inverse letters, empty words and zero exponent sum. The title incorrectly calls this a determinant character: in dimension d the determinant satisfies det rho(b)=R_1^{d e(b)} det rho_tilde(b). Replaced only determinant by scalar in the title, retaining the complete phase-tracking theorem and its source/dependency conventions.

The one-dimensional target C has all unit scalars as unit vectors, so the original Given incorrectly asserts uniqueness. Specified the concrete normalized target 1∈C. Controlled I fixes |+>⊗1 and controlled -I gives |->⊗1, with plus-outcome probabilities 1 and 0. The statement refuted and the full coherent-control witness remain unchanged; this is a nonfatal initial-state wording error.

The cited suppliers’ Remarks and proofs do contain the 24/63 Lie-word data, so those data are not invented. However the original joint proof never placed the initial pair (C5−C5^{-1},C8−C8^{-1}) in Lie(G), and its F1 contract quotes only separate-density Statements. This is a fatal logical gap in the simultaneous-closure argument. The repair uses only those separate-density Statements: common irrational-angle powers give a simultaneous circle and nonzero tangent; each projected Lie space is a nonzero SU(n)-invariant ideal, hence is all su(n). Finite determinant image, the proved nonisomorphic simplicity argument, and IFT/connectedness then give SU(5)×SU(8).

The general lemma quantifies over arbitrary dense Gamma; a Fibonacci-specific density theorem cannot supply that hypothesis for every Gamma. F2 now follows explicitly from the Given density assumption. Removed the unused specialized dependency and updated dependency_level to 9 (the covering supplier is level 8). The covering-sheet proof is sound: S0∩O is nonempty open, its image is nonempty open and meets Gamma, and the unique sheet lift lies in O. ACω and the full-inverse-image, rather than selected-lift, conclusion are retained.

Verification 2.1 wrongly attributes circle closures to the individual Fibonacci generators. Their eigenvalue ratio r=e^{-3πi/5} has order 10, so each generated projective cyclic subgroup is finite. The actual density supplier proves density via the irrational-angle word B1 B2^{-1} and its conjugate. Since F2 already supplies the full density conclusion, this is a nonfatal false explanatory sentence; replaced it with direct application of F2, retaining the conditional Majorana–Ising finite-image comparison.
